The sessions end with three folders that work. This page is the part after
that: a checklist to keep track of what you have tried, in the order that tends
to pay off. Stage 1 comes first. After it, the stages are independent, so pick
the one that matches the work in front of you.

Ticks are saved in your browser, on this device only. Nobody else sees them.

## Make the sessions yours {#stage-1}

[Stage 1 · do this first]{.stage-label}

Running a session on the sample proves the setup. Running it on your own files
is where you find out what you would change.

::: {#next-stage-1 .checklist progress="true"}
- [ ] Run [`/proposal-to-slides`](01_slidemaker/session-1.qmd) on a proposal of your own
- [ ] Run [`/collect`, `/synthesize` and `/report`](02_summarizer/session-2.qmd) on a folder of your own, one step at a time
- [ ] Run [`/researcher` and `/reviewer`](03_multitudes/session-3.qmd) on a strategy or plan of your own, and correct the briefing at the checkpoint
- [ ] Change one default in a session's `CLAUDE.md` (a page limit, a colour, the language) and run it again
- [ ] Open one recipe in a session's `skills/` folder and read it top to bottom
- [ ] Read `output/audit-log.md` from Session 3 once, start to finish
:::

## Build your first skill {#stage-2}

[Stage 2]{.stage-label}

The sessions gave you skills someone else wrote. The habit worth having is
noticing when one of your own tasks deserves one.
[Build your own skill](build-a-skill.qmd) walks through each line below.

::: {#next-stage-2 .checklist progress="true"}
- [ ] Notice a task you have explained to Claude three times
- [ ] Do it once more in plain conversation, and write down every correction you make
- [ ] Ask Claude to turn that conversation into a skill in `.claude/skills/`
- [ ] Open a fresh session and run the skill on a real input
- [ ] Add a review gate before it writes the final file
- [ ] Move anything you would tune later (lengths, folders, formats) into `CLAUDE.md`
:::

## Keep your skills working {#stage-3}

[Stage 3]{.stage-label}

A skill is a plain-English file, so it drifts: your needs change, the tools
improve, and steps that were necessary become clutter. Fixing one is a
conversation, not a rewrite. See
[When a skill disappoints](build-a-skill.qmd#when-a-skill-disappoints).

::: {#next-stage-3 .checklist progress="true"}
- [ ] Fix a skill right after a run that disappointed, while the bad output is still in the folder
- [ ] Ask Claude which steps in a skill it no longer needs, and remove them
- [ ] Review all the skills in a project at once: which overlap, which are broken, which could be simpler
:::

## Get a second opinion {#stage-4}

[Stage 4]{.stage-label}

Session 3's point is that the one who judges should not be the one who
gathered. You can borrow that for any draft, without building a pipeline.

::: {#next-stage-4 .checklist progress="true"}
- [ ] Ask for a review by an agent that sees only the draft, not the conversation that produced it
- [ ] Ask what the most important question a sceptical reader would raise is, before you send something
- [ ] Open a session folder in Codex (each one ships an `AGENTS.md`) and compare its output with Claude's
:::

A prompt for the first one:

```text
Start a new agent with a clean context. Give it only output/draft.md, not our
conversation. Ask it to list the three weakest claims in the draft and, for
each, what evidence would be needed to keep it. Show me its answer unedited.
```

## Pick up where you left off {#stage-5}

[Stage 5]{.stage-label}

A long conversation gets narrower (see [Tips](tips.qmd#while-you-work)), and a
new one starts from zero. A short handoff file bridges the two.

::: {#next-stage-5 .checklist progress="true"}
- [ ] End a working session by asking Claude to write a handoff note
- [ ] Start the next session by asking Claude to read it
- [ ] Move anything in the note that will stay true for weeks into `CLAUDE.md`
:::

```text
Write HANDOFF.md in this folder: what we were doing, what is finished, what is
still open, which files matter, and the next step. Keep it under one page.
```

```text
Read HANDOFF.md and tell me where we are before doing anything.
```

::: {.credit-note}
The tick-off format and the staging are adapted from Chris Blattman's
[claudeblattman.com](https://claudeblattman.com/), a guide to agents for people
who do not code. Worth reading alongside this one.
:::
